source.title: FedCARE: Federated Unlearning with Conflict-Aware Projection and Relearning-Resistant Recovery
source.authors: Yue Li; Mingmin Chu; Xilei Yang; Da Xiao; Ziqi Xu; Wei Shao; Qipeng Song; Hui Li

page_placements.theme: Image classifiers, encoders and federated models: approximate unlearning leaves recoverable information

record.file_problem: The main paper is present, but some extracted figure and table content is garbled or flattened, and the referenced supplementary material is not included.
record.tranche_reason: It tests post-unlearning recovery and whether recovery procedures restore an implanted backdoor, using federated recovery and attack-success rate rather than the LLM unlearning methods and attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures backdoor ASR after unlearning and recovery, including a standard FedAvg recovery ablation. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, prompt-only recovery, or the listed LLM unlearning methods. Other results about U-Acc, MIA, utility, and ordinary post-unlearning backdoor defense do not establish recovery by the attacks in the claim. Table 5 results for M1 and M2 are left out because they alter the generator or unlearning projection rather than the recovery mechanism; the paper attributes M1's ASR to the generator and does not describe M2 as a recovery test.
record.test_reason: A federated-unlearning method paper on CNN/ResNet-18 image classifiers (MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR). It uses post-unlearning relearning as motivation and reports its own method against ablated variants. The claim concerns LLM unlearning of hidden knowledge, so no row measures the same behaviour in the same kind of system. The recovery ablation also never reports backdoor ASR right after unlearning and before recovery. So the 45.77% under FedAvg recovery cannot show whether recovery restored the backdoor or unlearning never removed it.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude FedCARE gives low-overhead forgetting, better utility retention and less relearning during recovery than FU baselines. Their evidence on relearning is Table 5's backdoor ASR ablation alone, with no pre-recovery baseline.
record.recipe_differences: Federated image-classification unlearning and recovery, rather than LLM unlearning; evaluates backdoor ASR rather than targeted LLM knowledge accuracy and recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery outcome changes with backbone freezing and server-side vector filtering; the M4 ASR value differs between Table 5 and the accompanying prose.

fits_no_version.finding: In federated CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 unlearning, standard FedAvg recovery on the remaining clients leaves a 45.77% backdoor ASR. Freezing the backbone and filtering the rollback direction gives 0% ASR (Table 5). There is no post-unlearning, pre-recovery ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In federated image-classifier unlearning, continued training on retained clients can re-establish an unlearned backdoor; constraining recovery updates prevents this.

record.problems: The recovery evidence is limited to backdoor ASR in a non-IID CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 experiment; it does not establish recovery or resistance for general knowledge or LLMs. The M4 ASR is inconsistent between the table (29.60%) and prose (36.60%). No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 M1 and M2 ASR results are omitted because the paper describes them as generator and unlearning-projection ablations, not tests of recovery mechanisms. Other utility, privacy, efficiency, and ordinary unlearning results do not measure the recovery behavior in the claim.

untested.parts: No LLM unlearning or WMDP-style knowledge accuracy; no attack on retained knowledge.
No LLM relearning attack with a small unrelated, related or forget-subset set.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
FedCARE is not evaluated against the claim's attacks on LLMs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to nonexistent versions V2/V6, and its labels for B and F are not supported: the system is not an LLM, and there is no pre-recovery baseline. The M4 ASR differs between table (29.60%) and text (36.60%). Table 5's FedCARE U-ACC and MIA columns appear swapped.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports targeted-task accuracy and utility, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks fail after unlearning.

Recovery is continued federated training on remaining clients, not a specified small relearning set; it does not compare unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact subsets. The recovery outcome is backdoor ASR, not general LLM knowledge accuracy.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis distinguishing blocked access from deleted knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context prompting recovery experiment.

Tests post-unlearning federated recovery and recovery-component ablations for an implanted backdoor; does not test resistance to direct fine-tuning attacks using small data, activation edits, quantization, or prompting.

rows.measure: Backdoor attack success rate (ASR) after recovery
rows.note: The text describes this as severe relearning during recovery. ASR shows recovery of the implanted backdoor behavior, not general knowledge recovery.
rows.check: ResNet-18 federated image classifier with backdoor ASR, not LLM targeted knowledge. Version labels V2/V6 are invalid. No pre-recovery (post-unlearning) ASR baseline is given, so a 45.77% ASR after FedAvg recovery cannot be read as recovery.

relation.reason: Uses the relearning-during-recovery finding to motivate its design and reports only its own method and ablations, in a non-LLM setting.

tranche.reason: Federated image-classification method paper (CNN/ResNet-18 on MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR). It uses relearning during recovery as motivation and reports only its own method against baselines and ablations. It does not test LLM targeted-knowledge unlearning.

source_check.notes: Table 5 ASR column (M1-M5, FedCARE) reads 33.50, 0.00, 45.77, 29.60, 20.71, 0.00. M4 is 36.60% in the prose. No pre-recovery ASR. In the extracted Table 5, FedCARE's U-ACC (50.38%) and MIA (78.52%) look swapped: Sec. 4.2 gives client-level U-Acc 78.52% and MIA 50.38%.

statements.problem: None. M3 45.77% and FedCARE 0.00% match Table 5 (non-IID CIFAR-10, ResNet-18). Section 3.3 confirms recovery runs on the remaining clients, with the server filtering head updates along the rollback direction. The text reports no pre-recovery ASR.

reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 non-IID; recovery by standard FedAvg or recovery ablations without all FedCARE constraints
reader_labels.reason: ASR rises after recovery, with the paper describing relearning or residual rollback; this is evidence for recovery of the implanted backdoor behavior in this setting (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FedCARE recovery on CIFAR-10 non-IID with both backbone freezing and server-side vector filtering
reader_labels.reason: FedCARE reports 0.00% ASR after recovery, which the authors describe as complete backdoor removal (R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: ASR rebounds when recovery constraints are removed, indicating that the reported resistance depends on those components (R2–R3).
